newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Mercury ups offers for Power NZ shares.
newsitem.headline: Mercury ups offers for Power NZ shares.

text.p: Mercury Energy Ltd said on Thursday it had raised its offered price range for Power New Zealand shares held by Hamilton-based WEL Energy and local authorities.
Mercury said the price offered may be increased within a range of NZ$10-15 for each Power NZ share, up from its previous offer made on September 16 of NZ$7.25-$10 per share.
The oral offers will be for a maximum of 12.1 million shares, or eight percent of PNZ, which would raise Mercury's stake in the company to 40.6 percent.
The offers will be made to the WEL Energy Group and to the district councils of Thames-Coromandel, Matamata-Piako, South Waikato, Hauraki, Waipa, the Western Bay of Plenty and Waikato.
The eight local authorities own 7.1 percent of Power New Zealand.
Auckland-based Mercury is waging a long-running battle for Power NZ shares with Utilicorp New Zealand, which is 79 percent owned by Utilicorp United Inc.
